title: RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve Iterative Framework for Comprehensive Retrieval
claim: Iteratively retrieving, verifying, and re-querying with verified evidence recovers answers a single retrieval pass misses.
layout: Top query banner, then zig-zag flow of boxes and document strips with arrows
description: A gray banner at the top gives an example query, "Who are the directors of movies produced by Eric Newman?", with three color-coded answers: y1 blue, y2 yellow, y3 red. Below it, a zig-zag flow begins at the query q, which feeds a yellow Initial Retriever. That retriever outputs a row of five document icons, some tinted blue or yellow and some blank. These pass through a green Verifier box. The verified set shows green checks on the answer-bearing documents and red crosses on the blank ones. The checked documents are concatenated with q (⊕) and sent to a blue Subsequent Retriever. Its output row contains one red document, the new answer y3. A Final Output box merges the verified documents with the new red one. The color coding lets the eye follow each answer through the stages.
caption: Overview of our Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve framework. Each query $q$ aims to retrieve documents to get multiple answers $(y_1, y_2,y_3)$. The initial retriever takes a query and returns document sets, and the verifier examines each document, identifying two valid answers $y_1, y_2$. The subsequent retriever takes the query and documents containing identified answers as input, targeting to retrieve complementary answer $y_3$.
abstract: Comprehensively retrieving diverse documents is crucial to address queries that admit a wide range of valid answers. We introduce retrieve-verify-retrieve (RVR), a multi-round retrieval framework designed to maximize answer coverage. Initially, a retriever takes the original query and returns a candidate document set, followed by a verifier that identifies a high-quality subset. For subsequent rounds, the query is augmented with previously verified documents to uncover answers that are not yet covered in previous rounds. RVR is effective even with off-the-shelf retrievers, and fine-tuning retrievers for our inference procedure brings further gains. Our method outperforms baselines, including agentic search approaches, achieving at least 10% relative and 3% absolute gain in complete recall percentage on a multi-answer retrieval dataset (QAMPARI). We also see consistent gains on two out-of-domain datasets (QUEST and WebQSP) using different base retrievers. Our work presents a promising iterative approach for comprehensive answer recall leveraging a verifier and adapting retrievers to a new inference scenario.
